events.title: Elizabeth I Is Crowned Queen of England
events.description: In a ceremony at Westminster Abbey, Elizabeth I was crowned queen. She was 25 and had taken the throne after the death of her half-sister Mary I.
events.significance: Her 44-year reign gave its name to the Elizabethan era. England became a major naval power and saw a flowering of English culture, including Shakespeare.

events.title: The British Museum Opens Its Doors
events.description: The British Museum opened to the public in Montagu House in Bloomsbury, London. It was one of the first national museums in the world.
events.significance: It set a model for public access to human knowledge and heritage. Its collections now span millions of objects from across the globe.

events.title: Rosa Luxemburg and Karl Liebknecht Are Murdered
events.description: During the turmoil of the German Revolution, the Marxist leaders Rosa Luxemburg and Karl Liebknecht were killed in Berlin by far-right paramilitary soldiers.
events.significance: Their deaths weakened the German left and exposed the violence that undermined the Weimar Republic in its early days.

events.title: Wikipedia Goes Live
events.description: The free, collaboratively written online encyclopedia launched on the internet. It came less than a year after its predecessor, Nupedia, struggled to gain traction.
events.significance: Wikipedia grew into one of the most visited websites in the world. It changed how people find and share knowledge.

events.title: Miracle on the Hudson
events.description: US Airways Flight 1549 lost power in both engines after hitting a flock of Canada geese. Captain Chesley Sullenberger and First Officer Jeffrey Skiles glided it to a landing on the Hudson River in New York City.
events.significance: All 155 people aboard survived. The event is celebrated as one of the most successful ditchings in aviation history and a showcase of pilot skill and crew coordination.
